                    ### Question
                    A 70-year-old male with a 10-year history of COPD visits his pulmonologist for a checkup. Physical examination reveals cyanosis, digital clubbing, and bilateral lung wheezes are heard upon auscultation. The patient has a cough productive of thick yellow sputum. Which of the following findings is most likely present in this patient?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Decreased arterial carbon dioxide content
opb. Increased pulmonary arterial resistance
opc. Increased pH of the arterial blood
opd. Increased cerebral vascular resistance
ope. Increased right ventricle compliance

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
In a patient with COPD, chronic hypoxemia can lead to pulmonary vasoconstriction, resulting in increased pulmonary arterial resistance. Additionally, chronic hypoxemia can cause alveolar hypoventilation and retention of carbon dioxide, leading to decreased arterial carbon dioxide content. Therefore, the most likely finding in this patient is decreased arterial carbon dioxide content (Option A).
